results.title: Data Lifecycle - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
results.content: The first group is data , which can be detailed into (1a) data characteristics , such as data types, data formats, data sources, data volumes, data quality, data topics and data categories, data dynamism, (1b) data infrastructure , which covers technical equipment, including network and scalability and architecture and environment, as well as platforms, tools and sources, including their features and capabilities, management, security, guidelines and support, and technical standards encompassing various aspects including data formats, protocols, metadata schemas, and semantic standards that focus on encoding meaning into data, adhering to common vocabularies, ontologies, and semantic models, allowing for the explicit representation of concepts, relationships, and semantics within dataset, enabling effective data exchange, discovery, and utilisation, (1c) data lifecycle that includes data acquisition, data publication, data sharing, data storing / archiving, data accessing, data processing (including exploration), data use and data reuse, 5 5 data use refers to the initial utilisation of data (incl., accessing, analysing, interpreting, and deriving insights from data), while data reuse refers to the broader repurposing of data of data beyond its original purpose or context (incl., sharing, integrating, or combining data with other datasets or applications to generate additional value or insights).

results.title: A Pragmatic CDO's Field Guide to Data Quality — Part 2 — ...
results.content: We unpack a five-family taxonomy — business semantics & policy, identity/linkage (MDM), schema & pipeline, analytics & ML, governance & process — anchored in real-world outages. You’ll learn the signature failure modes (schema evolution gone wrong, CDC retractions, grain mismatches, missing consent flags), how to tag them for faster triage, and how to trace root cause with lineage so your post-mortems stop sounding like guesswork. * **Five Failure Families:** We catalog data quality failures into five families — (A) **Business Semantics & Policy**, (B) **Identity & Linkage (MDM)**, © **Technical Schema & Pipeline**, (D) **Analytics & ML**, (E) **Governance & Process** — with codes A1–A4, B1–B4, C1–C11, D1–D5, E1–E7. * **Symptom → Tag → Trace:** For each sub-code, we show how issues **surface** (symptoms like conflicting KPIs or duplicate records), how to **tag** incidents with the right code, and how to **trace** root cause via **data lineage**. Dr. Adnan Masood is an Engineer, Thought Leader, Author, AI/ML PhD, Stanford Scholar, Harvard Alum, Microsoft Regional Director, and STEM Robotics Coach.

results.title: A Cloud-Based Platform for Harmonized COVID-19 Data
results.content: Objective: We aim to present the design, implementation, and capabilities of the RADx Data Hub, a cloud-based platform developed to support findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable (FAIR) data practices and enable secondary analyses of the COVID-19–related data contributed by a nationwide network of researchers. Data producers, including individual study investigators and research groups, transmit their study data to one of the 4 (C)DCCs. These (C)DCCs, each aligned with a specific focus within the RADx initiative, play a critical role in the pipeline by standardizing, harmonizing, and preparing the data for inclusion in the Data Hub. After submission to the Data Hub, the data undergo automated validation to detect quality issues, such as nonadherence to standards, incorrect formats, or incomplete metadata.
